subject: Mode choice and latency/throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <j.lee@cartwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Mode choice and latency/throughput follow-up

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have everything on the record and can pick the right pilot path: 

- Traffic profile: steady baseline ~120 QPS with 10x marketing-driven bursts up to ~1,200 QPS for 1–2 hour windows.
- Latency targets: P95 goal <= 80 ms; P99 ideally < 150 ms for user-facing recommendations.
- Payloads: average request ~450 tokens, peak ~1,200 tokens for long sessions.
- Data constraints: no on-prem requirement today; PCI-sensitive flows are tokenized and sent to your payment backend.

Initial recommendation: start with Hosted API pilot configured for aggressive autoscaling and prefix caching (fastest time-to-value). If sustained sustained baseline or sustained bursts push consistent P99 tail latency above ~120–150 ms in production, we should transition to a Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) to gain deterministic throughput and lower tail latency.

Could you confirm the sustained baseline during business hours (is 120 QPS representative of 9am–5pm PST?) and whether those marketing bursts are predictable (calendar-driven) or ad-hoc? Also looping Marissa (ops) — can you validate capacity/burst pricing expectations so I can share an initial quote?

I attached a short SLO matrix and our updated pricing deck for reference.

Next steps I propose:
- Jordan to confirm baseline window and burst cadence by EOD Thu 3/4.
- Redwood runs a short latency sensitivity sketch against a test dataset (we can provision a hosted pilot within 48 hours).
- If pilot shows >120 ms P99 consistently during burst windows, we scope Dedicated sizing and term proposal.

Thanks — look forward to lining this up.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments: cartwise_slo_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_pricing_v2.pdf (PDF)

From: Jordan Lee <j.lee@cartwise.com>

Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 15:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mode choice and latency/throughput follow-up

Thanks Karthik — good summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Baseline: 9am–9pm ET (we run US-wide windows) our baseline is closer to 200 QPS; the 120 number was an off-hours average I mentioned earlier.
- Bursts: typically calendar-driven campaigns and partner referrals; predictable and usually last 45–90 minutes. We also see occasional organic spikes that are unpredictable (~20% of bursts).
- Payloads: the 450-token average is accurate; the 1,200-token long sessions are about 5% of traffic.
- Procurement: looping in procurement@cartwise.com for contract and SOW next steps.

Can you give a ballpark on whether Hosted will likely meet our P95 <= 80 ms with 200 baseline + predictable bursts? If not, we want to know the delta in committed spend to go Dedicated.

Jordan Lee
Head of Product | Cartwise Inc.
j.lee@cartwise.com

Subject: Fwd: Mode choice and latency/throughput follow-up

Marissa / Rishi —

Jordan just confirmed baseline is ~200 QPS (9am–9pm ET) with predictable campaign bursts and occasional organic spikes. They asked for a ballpark on whether Hosted will meet P95 <= 80 ms at that load. I propose we run a quick sensitivity sketch on Hosted at 200 baseline + a 6x burst multiplier (1,200 QPS) with their token distribution.

Questions for you:
1) With current runtime kernels and caching, what P95 P99 envelope should we expect on Hosted for 450-token average / peaks to 1,200 tokens? Call out whether prefix caching will likely reduce steady-state CPU/GPU cycles for recommendations.
2) If Hosted shows borderline tail latency during bursts, what Dedicated configuration (GPU count / instance type) gets us reliably under P99 150 ms and P95 <= 80 ms? Include ETA and rough OPEX delta.

I need a short note by EOD so I can reply to Jordan with a realistic next-step (pilot vs straight-to-dedicated).

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <j.lee@cartwise.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cartwise.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mode choice and latency/throughput follow-up — next steps

Jordan — thanks for the quick details and looping procurement. Quick update after internal check: 

- Hosted pilot: we can provision a hosted pilot instance within 48 hours. With prefix caching and an aggressive continuous-batching policy we expect Hosted to meet P95 <= 80 ms for baseline 200 QPS for the vast majority of requests. That said, predictable bursts to 1,200 QPS will likely push P99 into the 120–180 ms band depending on token mix; prefix/KV cache will help for cacheable requests but not for all long sessions.
- Dedicated sizing: if Cartwise wants deterministic tail latency during burst windows, our estimate is a Dedicated pool sized at 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (we'll provide exact vCPU/GPU SKU recommendations in the SOW). That configuration should bring P99 under 150 ms and P95 comfortably under 80 ms even for heavier token tails. OPEX delta vs Hosted (fully burstable) is roughly +40–60% depending on commitment term and caching hit rate — Marissa will share a concise pricing delta.

Proposed path: 
1) Start with a 2-week Hosted pilot (we'll run synthetic burst tests matching your campaign cadence and provide a telemetry report).
2) If pilot P99 during test bursts exceeds 150 ms or business deems deterministic latency critical, we convert to a Dedicated sizing proposal and present a term-based discount.

Can you confirm we should schedule the pilot to start Friday 3/5? I'll send a short pilot runbook and the SLO matrix to procurement for signature.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
